_comment: Worked example: register a LOCAL DEV Google OAuth client (Google OAuth) in an isolated Cloud project and capture its client id/secret.
Built from a real hand-driven agent-browser session (comet profile, CDP 127.0.0.1:9222, --session comet).
Keys starting with '_' are ignored by pixel (not part of the Flow schema); they are documentation for humans.
HOW TO RUN
pixel flow save google-oauth-app --from-file crates/pixel-flow/examples/google-oauth-app.json

pixel flow run google-oauth-app --var accept_terms=true --var test_user_email=<test-user-address> --var contact_email=<contact-address> [--var project_id=my-local-dev-app] [--var google_api=drive.googleapis.com] [--var app_name='My Local Dev App']
OAUTH_ENV_OUT=./.env.oauth crates/pixel-flow/examples/oauth-env.py capture google
OAUTH_CALLBACK_URL=<the callback_url you used> OAUTH_ENV_OUT=./.env.oauth crates/pixel-flow/examples/oauth-env.py check google
WHAT IT DOES: (create project if missing) > enable the API in google_api (default Drive) > consent screen wizard (External) > add test user >
create Web-application OAuth client with redirect URI callback_url (default http://localhost:3000/oauth/google/callback).
SCOPE: google_scope (default https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.readonly) is INFORMATIONAL. A Google OAuth client has no scopes; your app
requests them at authorize time. Change google_scope and google_api together if you need a different API (e.g. calendar-json.googleapis.com).
SAFETY: this creates an ISOLATED dev project (default id my-local-dev-app) and never touches an app that is under Google verification
or published. It stops if the audience page shows a 'Back to testing' button (production).
TESTING MODE: External apps in Testing publishing status issue refresh tokens that EXPIRE AFTER 7 DAYS, and only the listed test users can authorize.
Re-authorize weekly, or move to verified production separately (out of scope here).
TERMS: accept_terms defaults to false. Only accept_terms=true ticks 'I agree to the Google API Services: User Data Policy'.
Without it the flow stops at the wizard's Finish step and nothing is configured.
THE SECRET: the 'OAuth client created' dialog shows client id + secret. Newer consoles may NOT let you view the secret again after
closing the dialog, so capture before closing it. Do NOT click 'Download JSON'. pixel-flow cannot write files and `pixel flow run`
discards `eval` output, so oauth-env.py reads the dialog straight into $OAUTH_ENV_OUT (mode 600) and prints only lengths.
It writes OAUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / OAUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET. `check google` POSTs a bogus code to oauth2.googleapis.com/token:
anything except invalid_client (normally invalid_grant) means the client credentials are accepted.
LOGIN IS OUT OF SCOPE. The comet session must already be signed in to Google. A redirect to accounts.google.com (confirmidentifier) or a
'Verify it's you' prompt makes the flow STOP on purpose (a `click` whose ref_hint can never match). It never clicks Next or types credentials.
EMAILS: test_user_email and contact_email are REQUIRED vars with no default; the flow never embeds an email. NOTE pixel's `flow run` log echoes
typed values, so the addresses you pass appear in that local log. The 'User support email' is the first combobox option (the signed-in account).
PARAMETER QUIRK: project-scoped URLs are built in page JS because only value_var resolves declared defaults; the JS repeats the default
project id (my-local-dev-app). If you change the var default, change it in the nav eval steps too, or always pass --var project_id.
NOT IDEMPOTENT: re-running adds another OAuth client (the project, API and consent screen steps are skipped when already done).
AFTER THE FLOW (manual follow-up): your backend/app reads OAUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / OAUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET from its
process environment. `source` the env file written to $OAUTH_ENV_OUT before starting the API. Never commit that file.
NEVER put real client ids or secrets in this file.
name: google-oauth-app
title: Create a local-dev Google OAuth client and capture client id/secret
description: In an isolated Cloud project (default my-local-dev-app): creates it if missing, enables the API in google_api (default Drive), configures an External consent screen in Testing mode, adds a test user, and creates a Web-application OAuth client (default name 'My Local Dev App') with the local callback_url, ending on the one-time 'OAuth client created' dialog. Follow immediately with `oauth-env.py capture google` to write OAUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / OAUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET to $OAUTH_ENV_OUT (mode 600), then `oauth-env.py check google`. The User Data Policy checkbox is gated behind --var accept_terms=true (default false). Testing-mode refresh tokens expire after 7 days. Login is out of scope; the flow stops if signed out. Not idempotent for the client.
preconditions: Verify comet-cdp is up (port 9222) and `agent-browser --session comet tab list` answers
The comet browser profile is ALREADY signed in to the Google account that should own the dev project (this flow never types credentials or clicks Next on sign-in pages)
Read the Google API Services User Data Policy yourself; pass --var accept_terms=true only if you accept it (default false: the flow stops at the consent wizard's Finish step)
Pass --var test_user_email and --var contact_email as real addresses (required, no default; the flow stops if they are empty or malformed)
Export OAUTH_ENV_OUT=<path> before the capture step (the file receives secrets: keep it out of git, mode 600 is enforced)

vars.name: app_name
vars.description: Consent-screen app name and OAuth client name

vars.name: homepage_url
vars.description: Accepted for a uniform interface with the other oauth-app flows; the recorded Google flow needed no homepage, so it is unused

vars.name: callback_url
vars.description: Authorized redirect URI your local app's OAuth callback route listens on

vars.name: project_id
vars.description: Cloud project id/name to create or reuse (the id is the slug of the name). Project-scoped URLs are built in page JS that repeats this default

vars.name: google_api
vars.description: API service name to enable (changeable, e.g. calendar-json.googleapis.com). Page JS repeats this default for an omitted var

vars.name: google_scope
vars.description: INFORMATIONAL, changeable: the scope your app will request at authorize time. A Google OAuth client does not declare scopes, so the flow does not type it anywhere

vars.name: test_user_email
vars.description: Email added as a Testing-mode test user (only listed users can authorize while the app is in Testing)

vars.name: contact_email
vars.description: Developer contact email for the consent-screen wizard (step 3)

vars.name: accept_terms
vars.description: 'true' ticks 'I agree to the Google API Services: User Data Policy' on your behalf. Anything else (including omitted) leaves it unticked and the flow stops at the Finish step. Must be passed with --var; it has no effective default

steps.rationale: Open the Cloud console credentials page (no project param yet). May redirect to accounts.google.com when signed out.
steps.on_failure: If the open times out, re-run `agent-browser --session comet tab list` and retry once

steps.rationale: The console is a heavy SPA; let it (or a login redirect) settle
Login is out of scope. A redirect to accounts.google.com (confirmidentifier) means signed out: stop before touching any Next button or field.

then.rationale: STOP: redirected to accounts.google.com. Sign in by hand in Comet, then re-run this flow. Never click Next or type here. (Fails on purpose: the ref_hint can never match, so the flow aborts with this message.)
then.ref_hint: STOP - Google sign-in required in the comet session - a human must sign in, then re-run the flow

steps.rationale: Re-verification page rendered inside the console (Verify its you). Same rule: stop.
steps.condition: page shows 'Verify it' or 'Choose an account' or 'Enter your email'

then.rationale: STOP: Google is asking to verify the account. A human must complete it in Comet, then re-run this flow.
then.ref_hint: STOP - Google Verify-its-you prompt in the comet session - a human must complete it, then re-run the flow

steps.rationale: GUARD: test_user_email and contact_email are REQUIRED with no default. An omitted var is rejected by pixel; an empty or malformed one is caught here and flagged for the next step.
Stop with a clear message if an email var is empty or malformed, BEFORE anything is created.

then.rationale: STOP: test_user_email and contact_email must be passed as real email addresses (--var test_user_email=<address> --var contact_email=<address>). Nothing was created.
then.ref_hint: STOP - set test_user_email and contact_email to real addresses with --var, then re-run the flow

steps.rationale: Go to the credentials page of the TARGET project (project_id, default my-local-dev-app). If that project does not exist the console falls back to /projectselector2/..., handled next. Unverified: how the console reacts to a nonexistent ?project= value.
Let the page load
CREATE PROJECT only if it does not exist: with no usable project the console shows /projectselector2/... with a 'Create project' button.

then.rationale: Open the new-project form
Let the New Project form render
Capture the form: 'Project name' textbox (prefilled like 'My Project 12345'), Organization/Location, Create
PITFALL (append): the name is PREFILLED and real typing APPENDS to it, so use `fill` (replaces) and verify. The project ID is derived from the name as a slug (my-local-dev-app).
Verify the name AND the generated Project ID line before creating
Verify the name took. NOTE: {{project_id}} only substitutes when passed with --var; with the default this reads as not met and the fallback re-enters it, which is harmless.

otherwise.rationale: Select all so typing REPLACES the prefill (macOS shortcut)
Real key typing over the selection

then.rationale: Create the project. The default Organization is fine.
Project creation takes a while; the id then appears as ?project=<id> in the URL
Reload the credentials page scoped to the new project
Let the page load

steps.rationale: Confirm the credentials page of the target project is showing (URL has ?project=<id>)
Open the API library page for google_api (default drive.googleapis.com) in the project
steps.value: (()=>{const raw='{{project_id}}';const id=raw.startsWith('{{')?'my-local-dev-app':raw;const a='{{google_api}}';const api=a.startsWith('{{')?'drive.googleapis.com':a;setTimeout(()=>{location.href='https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/library/'+encodeURIComponent(api)+'?project='+encodeURIComponent(id)},50);return 'navigating to API library page for '+api+' in project '+id})()

steps.rationale: Let the API page load
Enable the API only if it is not enabled yet (an enabled API no longer shows the enable button).

then.rationale: Enable the API. Lands on /apis/api/<api>/metrics with a 'Disable API' button.
Enabling takes a few seconds
Expect the metrics page with a 'Disable API' button (proof the API is enabled)

steps.rationale: Open the consent-screen wizard directly. PITFALL: the 'Get started' link on the overview points here but clicking the link itself did not navigate.
Let the wizard load
Run the 4-step wizard only when it is showing (already-configured projects skip straight to Audience).

then.rationale: Focus 'App name' (click+type works here; fill does not register)
Type the app name
Open the 'User support email' combobox. PITFALL: its listbox does NOT appear in the accessibility tree.
Enter takes the FIRST option, which is the signed-in account. Do not try to click an option: it is not in the snapshot.
Verify the 'User support email' combobox now shows an account

Best-effort verification that the combobox holds an email (throws if empty, which aborts the flow when agent-browser reports the exception; the email itself is not returned or logged). If it fails: reopen the combobox, press ArrowDown, then Enter, and re-run from the wizard.
then.on_failure: Reopen the combobox, press ArrowDown, then Enter; verify the combobox value by eye (do not copy it anywhere)

then.rationale: Wizard step 1 -> 2 (Audience)
Let step 2 render

Audience: choose External. The project org differs from the user's Workspace domain; External + Testing needs no Google verification. (Internal would be rejected.) The two quoted terms require a radio line that also says External.
Wizard step 2 -> 3 (Contact Information)
Let step 3 render
PITFALL: 'Text field for emails' is a CHIP input. Type the contact email (real key events), then press Enter to commit the chip.
Enter commits the typed email as a chip; without it Next stays disabled
Wizard step 3 -> 4 (Finish)
Let step 4 render

TERMS GATE: tick 'I agree to the Google API Services: User Data Policy' ONLY when --var accept_terms=true was passed. Unset or any other value leaves it unchecked and Continue disabled (fail-closed: {{accept_terms}} is not defaulted, so an omitted var stays a literal and never equals 'true'). Passing accept_terms=true means the human accepts the policy.
then.value: (()=>{const txt=c=>[...(c.labels||[])].map(l=>l.innerText).join(' ')+' '+((c.closest('label')||c.parentElement||{}).innerText||'');const cb=[...document.querySelectorAll('input[type=checkbox]')].find(c=>/user data policy/i.test(txt(c)));if(!cb)return 'terms-checkbox-not-found';if('{{accept_terms}}'!=='true')return 'terms-NOT-accepted (accept_terms is not true): left unchecked';if(!cb.checked)cb.click();return 'terms-checked='+cb.checked})()

then.rationale: Click Continue (reports not-found-or-disabled instead of failing when the policy box is unticked)
Let the Create button appear
Click Create to finish the consent-screen wizard
Branding/audience config is saved server-side; give it time
Still on the Finish step means the policy was not accepted (accept_terms != true) or Create did not fire. Nothing was configured. Stop.

STOP: the consent-screen wizard is still open on the Finish step. Either accept_terms was not true (re-run with --var accept_terms=true after reading the Google API Services User Data Policy) or a required field is missing. (Fails on purpose.)
then.ref_hint: STOP - Google consent screen was not created - accept_terms must be true and every wizard step must be complete

steps.rationale: Open Audience (test users, publishing status)
Let the page load
Publishing status must read 'Testing'. (In production the page shows a 'Back to testing' button.)
Never alter an app that is already published: a 'Back to testing' button means production. Stop.

then.rationale: STOP: publishing status is not Testing (a 'Back to testing' button is showing). This flow only works on a Testing-mode dev project and never publishes or edits a production app.
then.ref_hint: STOP - Google app is not in Testing mode - this flow only works on a Testing-mode dev project

steps.rationale: Open the test-user dialog
Let the dialog render
PITFALL: 'Text field for emails' is a CHIP input: type the email (real key events), then Enter to commit it
Enter commits the chip
Save the test user
Let the save settle
Open the OAuth client creation form
Let the form load
Open the 'Application type' combobox. PITFALL: its listbox options are NOT in the plain snapshot.
Let the listbox open
'Web application' is the first option; Home then Enter selects it by keyboard (alternative: `agent-browser screenshot --annotate` refs)
Select the focused option
Let the Web-application fields render
Only the Web application type shows the 'Add URI' buttons (JavaScript origins, redirect URIs). If they are absent, the type was not selected: stop for a human.

otherwise.rationale: STOP: 'Web application' could not be selected by keyboard. Pick it by hand in Comet (or use `agent-browser screenshot --annotate`), then continue manually from the Name box.
otherwise.ref_hint: STOP - Google OAuth client type Web application not selected - a human must choose it

steps.rationale: PITFALL: Name is PREFILLED ('Web client 1'); use `fill` to replace it, then verify
Re-snapshot so the Name textbox shows its value
Verify the Name value took. NOTE: {{app_name}} only substitutes when passed with --var; with the default this reads as not met and the fallback re-enters it, which is harmless.

otherwise.rationale: Select all existing text so typing REPLACES it (macOS shortcut; use Control+a elsewhere)
Real key typing over the selection

steps.rationale: Add a redirect URI row: click the SECOND 'Add URI' button (the first belongs to Authorized JavaScript origins, which stay empty).
steps.value: (()=>{const bs=[...document.querySelectorAll('button')].filter(b=>/add uri/i.test(b.innerText));if(bs.length<2)return 'add-uri-buttons='+bs.length+' (expected 2: JavaScript origins, then Authorized redirect URIs)';bs[1].click();return 'clicked 2nd Add URI (redirect URIs)'})()

steps.rationale: Let the 'URIs 1' textbox render
Focus the redirect-URI box
PITFALL: REAL key typing is required; otherwise Create stays disabled
Verify the redirect URI is in the box and Create is enabled
Create the OAuth client. Opens an 'OAuth client created' dialog.
Let the dialog render

FLOW ENDS HERE with the 'OAuth client created' dialog open (client id like <digits>-<hash>.apps.googleusercontent.com, secret GOCSPX-...). Do NOT click 'Download JSON' and do NOT close the dialog: newer consoles may not show the secret again. NEXT: OAUTH_ENV_OUT=<path> crates/pixel-flow/examples/oauth-env.py capture google

success_signal: page text contains 'OAuth client created' (the one-time dialog is open). Then immediately run: OAUTH_ENV_OUT=<path> oauth-env.py capture google && oauth-env.py check google
